- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) or shows strong reversal, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion or sentiment-driven rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days after spike.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing short-term sentiment shifts; adjust for sentiment volatility: if sentiment swings > 0.3 in 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per swing.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend + negative sentiment, forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- Avoid over-reliance on recent history (last 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment) for 30d forecasts.
